newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's central bourse trims commission.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's central bourse trims commission.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse said on Monday it would trim commission charged to securities traders in a bid to help reduce overall trading costs.
Three types of new tariffs will be applied from August 19 to fully-listed and semi-regulated firms and bonds, the Zagreb Stock Exchange said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
Commission is divided into different classes depending on the size of transactions. It will be calculated on the basis of each trader's daily business and will be charged weekly.
Due to regulatory costs the highest levies, ranging from 0.05 to 0.35 percent, will be imposed on trade in fully-listed stocks.
The bourse hopes to stimulate liquidity by progressively decreasing charges as turnover rises. Bond trading carries a minimal commission of 0.01-0.2 percent.

In order to draw more business, the bourse first cut commission on large transactions in March. It completely renounced commission for a month between July 15 and August 15 to spur trade during traditionally lazy summer weeks. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
